Reading this map

What does a point on the map mark?

The named place in the report, not an exact impact point. Incidents from the IMO register are placed from their text and show their likely radius when selected.

What does claimed mean?

The event was reported by only one side and not confirmed by anyone else. Claimed events are drawn hollow and labeled as claimed on their card.

Why are ship attacks drawn at sea?

Ship attacks are drawn at the position the report gives, and at the nearest water when that place is on land, so a hit ship never sits on a coastline town.

What are the numbered circles?

Events close together on screen are drawn as one numbered group. Tap a group to list its events, and to zoom in when that would separate them.

How are naval missions drawn?

Mission areas are approximate outlines of published operating areas. Only missions under way on the day are drawn: today, or the day of the event you open.

How often is the list updated?

An automated review checks for new events every six hours and adds only those linked to a source. The stamp on the map shows when the list was last reviewed.
